tldr: With one discrete confounder cell per observation and any supplied maximal cell-effect deviation \(M\rho_n\), \(0\le\rho_n\le2\), the full-class minimax mean squared error is \(M^2\{n^{-1}+\rho_n^2/\log^2(e+n\rho_n^2)\}\). A total deterministic centered-factorial estimator attains this frontier, and a common-design binary prior proves the matching all-estimator converse. Exact homogeneity, the former critical radius, and the unrestricted model occur at \(\rho_n=0\), \(\rho_n=\log(en)/\sqrt n\), and \(\rho_n=2\), respectively; the exact-homogeneity endpoint also has the direct collision-regression estimator and two-point certificate proved here.
gap: The direct paper anchor proves the unrestricted and exact-homogeneity endpoints and explicitly leaves sharp dependence on maximal effect heterogeneity open. The closest same-class manuscript narrows the critical benchmark only to \(M^2/n\lesssim\mathsf R_n(M)\lesssim M^2\log^2(en)/n\).
